Land-birds of Galapagoes

1. Craxirex galapagoensis. I believe to be difft. from anything on the main.

2. Strix punctatissima occurs in Ecuador. I have examined speci- mens collected by Fraser at Quito.

3. Otus galapagoensis occurs in S.A. as I believe

4. Progne modesta I have never seen from the main.

5. Pyrocephalus nanus occurs in Ecuador (Fraser) at least I believe it the same

6 — dubius a doubtful species? probably = nanus.

7 Myiobius magnirostris, probably peculiar to Galapagoes

8

9 Three Mimi all peculiar but M. parvulus is hardly

10 separable fr. M. melanotis

11. ‘Wren’ Journal p. 378. I do not know what this is: not mentd.in Zool. of Beagle?

12. Zenaida galapagoensis probably occurs on mainland—

13–25—&Geospizinæ— I have every reason to believe this group of Finches quite peculiar to these islands and “Bow island” whence one was obtd. during voyage of the ‘Sulphur’ see Zool. of Sulphur p. 42

P. L. S.

My dear Sir

I thank you extremely for your list of the Galapagos Birds, & I trust that it will be in time for a note at end of my Journal, & will likewise do to correct the Origin of Species.—

The wren is Sylvicola aureola figured in Zoology of Beagle; I have assumed that it confined to the Archipelago. I am surprised that the Zenaida “probably occurs on Mainland”.—

Do you remember my asking you to be so very kind as to keep in mind & make memorandum for me of any cases of abnormal parts in Birds being variable. Will you kindly run your eye through enclosed list (& after having looked through it, tear it up) & then you will see the sort of cases, which interest me, & very grateful I shall be for any assistance on this head.—

With my best thanks for your kind assistance | Believe me | Yours sincerely | C. Darwin
